title: WPSB/316/2023 of KIRAN Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH ITS SECRETARY
respondent: STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH ITS SECRETARY
judges: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI,HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIVEK BHARTI SHARMA
head: I N THE HI GH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAI NI TAL HON'BLE THE ACTI NG CHI EF JUSTI CE MR. MANOJ KUMAR TI W ARI AND HON'BLE MR. VI VEK BHARTI SHARMA, J. W RI T PETI TI ON ( S/ B) No.3 1 6 of 2 0 2 3 Kiran ...Petitioner Versus State of Uttarakhand and others ...Respondents With W RI T PETI TI ON ( S/ B) No.1 7 5 of 2 0 2 3 Gopal Singh Gauniya & others ...Petitioners Versus State of Uttarakhand and others ...Respondents Counsel for the petitioners Counsel for State of Uttarakhand Counsel for Rehabilitation Counsel of India. Counsel for respondent no.5 Counsel for intervener Counsel for CBSE : Mr. Vinay Kum ar, learned counsel, Mr. K.N. Joshi, learned DAG, Mr. S.S. Chaudhary, learned Brief Holder, Ms.Puja Banga, learned Brief Holder. Mr. Saurav Adhikari, learned counsel. Mr. Yogesh Kum ar Pacholia, learned counsel. Mr. Dushyant Mainali, learned counsel. Mr. Shashank Upadhaya, learned counsel. JUDGMENT : (p er Mr . Man o j Ku m ar Tiw ar i, A.C.J.) Since comm on question of facts and law are involved in these writ petitions, therefore, these petitions are being heard and decided together. However, for the sake of brevity and convenience, facts of WPSB No.316 of 2023 are being considered and discussed.

paras.text: By m eans of writ petition being WPSB No.316 of 2023, petitioners have sought the following reliefs: - "I t is, therefore, m ost respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court m ay graciously be pleased to: (i) I ssue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Certiorari calling for the records and quashing Clause 2 (Educational Qualification) of the Executive Order dated 25.03.2023 issued by the Secretary, Elem entary Education, Govt. of Uttarakhand (Annexure No. 18. to the writ petition) to the extent it provides that the candidate should have com pulsorily qualified the Teacher Eligibility Test-I , however, the fact is that in the State of Uttarakhand, the agency nom inated by the State for conducting the TET-I Exam ination has not conducted the sam e for last m ore than 6 years by including the qualification of B.Ed. (Special Education) for the post of Assistant Teacher, Govt. Prim ary School. (ii) I ssue a writ order or direction in the nature of Certiorari quashing Clause 2 (Procedure for Selection) of the Executive Order dated 25.03.2023 issued by the Secretary, Elem entary Education, Govt. of Uttarakhand (Annexure No.1.8.to the writ petition) to the extent it provides that appointm ent the Assistant Teacher, Govt. Prim ary School (Special Education) will be based on the m erit of the Quality Points inasm uch the appointm ent of Assistant Teacher, Govt. Prim ary School as provided in Service Rules of 2012 as am ended from tim e to tim e is based on the m erit of year of passing of the Training Exam ination. (iii) I ssue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandam us directing the respondents to hold the Petitioners as eligible for the post of Assistant Teacher, Govt. Prim ary School (Special Education) based on the educational and training qualification of the Petitioners inasm uch as the Agency nom inated by the State Governm ent for conducting Teacher Eligibility Test-1 has not conducted Teacher Eligibility Test-I for last m ore than 6 years for the students having the qualification of B.Ed. (Special Education). (iv) I ssue any suitable writ, order or direction which this Hon'ble Court m ay deem fit and proper in the circum stances of the case.

The petitioners in the WPSB No.316 of 2023 possess B.Ed (Special Education) qualification, besides Bachelors Degree, but none of them has qualified Teachers Eligibility Test-1 (in short "TET-1"), which is now a necessary qualification for appointment as Teacher in any recognized Prim ary School.

According to the petitioners, TET-1 was never conducted by the agency nominated by State Government, for candidates having B.Ed (Special Education) qualification, and due to this reason, petitioners did not get the opportunity to appear in TET-1, therefore, on account of lapse on the part of State authorities, petitioners cannot be m ade to suffer and they cannot be held ineligible for appointment as Teacher in Governm ent Prim ary Schools.

I t is further contended on behalf of the petitioners that in the year 2017, Uttarakhand School Education Board, conducted TET-1 examination, however, petitioners and other persons with B.Ed (Special Education) qualification were not permitted to appear in the exam ination. Therefore, insistence on TET-1 as essential qualification for appointment as Prim ary School Teacher, according to the petitioners is unjust.

Petitioners have challenged executive instructions issued by Government of Uttarakhand on 25.03.2023. These instructions were issued in view of judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of " Raj n eesh Ku m ar Pan d ey an d ot h er s Vs. Un ion of I n d ia & ot h er s" reported in 2021 (17) SCC 1. The directions issued in the aforesaid judgment contained in paragraph 72, is extracted below: - "72. In view of the above, a m ultipronged approach needs to be adopted by the concerned Authorities with im m ediate effect, inter alia, as follows: 72.1. The Central Governm ent m ust forthwith notify the norm s and standards of pupil-teacher ratio for special schools and also separate norm s for special teachers who alone can im part education and training to CwSN in the general schools; and until such tim e, as a stopgap arrangem ent adopt the recom m endations m ade by the State Com m issioner, NCT of Delhi in the case of Ms. Reshm a Parveen reproduced in paras 65 and 66 above; 72.2. To create com m ensurate perm anent posts as per the just ratio to be specified by the com petent authority for the rehabilitation professionals/ special teachers who can cater to the needs of CwSN; 72.3. To initiate appointm ent process to fill-in vacancies for the posts so created for rehabilitation professionals/ special teachers for being appointed on regular basis. The sam e shall be com pleted within six m onths from the date of this order or before the com m encem ent of academ ic year 2022-2023, whichever is earlier; 72.4. To overcom e the shortage of resource persons (rehabilitation professionals/ special trained teachers), the training schools/ institutions m ust take steps to augm ent the num ber whilst ensuring that the norm s and standards specified under the governing laws and regulations including that of the Council for grant of recognition and registration are fulfilled; 72.5. Until sufficient num ber of special teachers becom es available for general schools and special schools, the services of special trained teachers can be availed as itinerant teachers as per the SSS within the school block (cluster schools) to optim ize the resource persons and as a stopgap arrangem ent; 72.6. The other teachers and staff in the general schools be given com pulsory training and sensitized to handle the CwSN in the general schools, if adm itted; 72.7. The authorities m ay also explore the possibility of m erging unviable special schools with relatively viable special schools in the neighbourhood, so as to entail in consolidation of assets and resources for better delivery to the requirem ents of CwSN."

The executive instructions issued by Government of Uttarakhand on 25.03.2023, provides that candidates who have qualified TET-1 alone were to be considered for appointm ent as Assistant Teacher (Special Education) in Governm ent Prim ary Schools. However, B.Ed (Special Education) was recognized as one of the qualification besides D.Ed (Special Education) or any qualification recognized by R.C.I. for appointm ent as Teacher in a Government Prim ary School.

Learned State Counsel, however, points out that Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of " Dev esh Sh ar m a Vs. Un ion of I n d ia & ot h er s" reported in 2 0 2 3 SCC On lin e SC 9 8 5 , has held that B.Ed is not a sufficient qualification for appointm ent as Teacher in Prim ary Schools.

I t is further contention of the State Counsel that B.Ed (Special Education) was never prescribed as sufficient qualification for appointm ent as Assistant Teacher in Governm ent Prim ary Schools, and persons with B.Ed (Special Education) degree are qualified to be appointed in Secondary Schools if they m eet other eligibility criterion for teaching children with special needs.

Learned State Counsel also refers to the recent judgment rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of " Nav in Ku m ar & ot h er s Vs. Un ion of I n d ia & ot h er s" reported in 2 0 2 4 SCC On lin e SC 2 3 6 0 , where also the earlier view was reiterated that B.Ed is not a qualification sufficient for appointm ent as Teachers in Government Prim ary School. Paragraph 12 of the aforesaid judgment is extracted below: - "12. In fact, we have been shown today an order of NCTE dated 04.09.2023 whereby the judgem ent in Devesh Sharm a (supra) was com m unicated to Chief Secretaries of all State Governm ents for further appropriate action. In spite of this, appointm ents were given to B.Ed. candidates which was illegal and has now rightly been quashed, by the Chhattisgarh High Court."

Learned State Counsel further submits that in view of the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of " Dev esh Sh ar m a Vs. Un ion of I n d ia & ot h er s" and reiterated in " Nav in Ku m ar & ot h er s Vs. Un ion of I n d ia & ot h er s" , with B.Ed (Special Education) qualification, petitioners cannot claim appointment as Prim ary School Teacher. He further submits that National Council for Teachers Education (in short "NCTE") in exercise of its power under section 23 of Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 has issued notification dated 23.08.2010, which provides that passing of TET is necessary for appointment as Teacher in a Prim ary School. Thus, he submits that since petitioners have not qualified TET, therefore, they cannot be considered for appointment in Government Prim ary Schools in view of the notification issued by NCTE dated 23.08.2010 and reiterated by subsequent notification issued by NCTE on 29.07.2011.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that since the agency, which was assigned the task of holding TET in State of Uttarakhand did not permit B.Ed (Special Education) qualification holders to appear in TET-1, therefore, penalizing the petitioners and other similarly situated candidates for lapse on the part of concerned agency is not proper, therefore, petitioners deserve to be permitted to participate in the ongoing selection process.

Learned State Counsel per contra submits that in terms of interim order passed by coordinate Bench on 20.07.2023, Uttarakhand School Education Board held TET-1 and all candidates with B.Ed. (Special Education) qualification, including petitioners and interveners had an opportunity to participate. However, only few of the petitioners could qualify in TET-1 and all others were declared unsuccessful. Thus, he submits that petitioners cannot blame the agency holding TET-1 for their inability to qualify the TET-1.

Learned State Counsel further submits that even the Service Rules framed in exercise of power under proviso to Article 309 of the Constitution of I ndia provide that passing of TET is one of the essential conditions of eligibility, therefore, anyone who has not passed T.E.T-1 is not eligible for appointment.

Learned counsel for the petitioners points out that the interveners also have not qualified TET-1 and they also possess B.Ed (Special Education) qualification, therefore, the interveners will sink or sail with the petitioners and they cannot claim any better right than the petitioners. We are not going into the issue as to whether petitioners or interveners have better claim for appointment.

We find force in the submission m ade by learned State Counsel that passing of TET-1 is one of the essential conditions of eligibility as per notification issued by NCTE, which was issued under Section 23 of Right of Children to Free and Com pulsory Education Act, 2009, therefore, anyone who has not qualified TET-1 cannot be considered for appointment in Prim ary Schools. Even otherwise also, in view of the judgm ent rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of " Dev esh Sh ar m a Vs. Un ion of I n d ia & ot h er s" and " Nav in Ku m ar & ot h er s Vs. Un ion of I n d ia & ot h er s" (supra) that there cannot be any direction in favour of B.Ed (Special Education) qualification holders, who have not qualified T.E.T-1 to consider their claim for appointment as Prim ary School Teacher in Governm ent Schools.

I n view of the above, the writ petitions fail and the same are dism issed. _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ MANOJ KUMAR TI W ARI , A.C.J. _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ VI VEK BHARTI SHARMA, J. Dt: 12th November, 2024 NR/ NITESH RAWAT

note.title: Kiran v. State of Uttarakhand & Ors. (WPSB/175/2023 ke saath)
note.summary: Uttarakhand HC, Division Bench (Acting CJ Manoj Kumar Tiwari aur Justice Vivek Bharti Sharma), 12.11.2024. B.Ed. (Special Education) wale umeedwaron ne TET-1 pass nahi kiya tha. Unhone Assistant Teacher (Special Education), primary ke 25.03.2023 ke executive order ko chunauti di thi.
note.held: TET-1 NCTE notification ke anusaar zaroori shart hai. Devesh Sharma (2023 SCC OnLine SC 985) aur Navin Kumar (2024 SCC OnLine SC 2360) ke baad B.Ed. primary teacher ke liye kaafi yogyata nahi maani ja sakti. Petitions dismissed.
use: Graduation % ka mudda yahan nahi hai, isliye yeh Sateshwari ke mukhya tark ke khilaaf nahi jaata.
caution: Agar Sateshwari ki niyukti primary (class I–V) mein B.Ed. ke aadhaar par hui hai, to State Devesh Sharma ka tark utha sakti hai (para 8, 10, 16). Niyukti ka level, TET aur training ki sthiti pehle se pakki kar lein.
Para 11 mein State ka tark: NCTE ki 23.08.2010 aur 29.07.2011 ki notifications ke anusaar TET zaroori hai.
